original_question: Can one solve the equation d-bar u = f with sup-norm estimates on smooth bounded convex domains in C^2?
target_in_paper: Nearest paper-faithful target: the open problem in arXiv:math/9509202 (The Several Complex Variables Problem List) concerning whether sup-norm estimates for the \bar\partial-equation hold on convex domains in \mathbb{C}^2. The arXiv record itself shows this source is a problem list rather than a theorem/proposition paper.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the operator equation \bar\partial u=f, the desired type of estimate (sup-norm / L^\infty control), and the geometric setting of smooth bounded convex domains in \mathbb{C}^2. Those are the core ingredients of the intended problem.
missing_details: It should specify that the data f is a (0,1)-form, not an arbitrary function or distribution.

It should state the integrability/regularity class of f relevant to a sup-norm estimate, namely bounded coefficients (equivalently an L^\infty_{(0,1)} datum), together with the condition \bar\partial f=0.
It should make explicit that the question is quantified for every smoothly bounded convex domain \Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^2.
It should state that one seeks a bounded solution u, not merely some weak or distributional solution.
It should spell out the estimate itself, i.e. whether one asks for the existence of a constant C_\Omega such that \|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}.
It should clarify that the constant is allowed to depend on the domain \Omega but not on f.

It should distinguish the problem from neighboring finite-type or real-analytic-boundary results; the intended question is about convex domains in \mathbb{C}^2 as such, not a broader class of pseudoconvex domains.
refined_question: Let \Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^2 be a smoothly bounded convex domain. Is it true that there exists a constant C_\Omega>0 such that for every bounded \bar\partial-closed (0,1)-form f on \Omega, one can find a bounded function u on \Omega with \bar\partial u=f and \|u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\,\|f\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}?
justification: arXiv:math/9509202 is not a conventional theorem paper; it is a problem list. The draft does not match the metadata-only labels Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 mentioned in your instructions, which are not present in the accessible arXiv record for this ID. The mathematically nearest paper-faithful reading is the longstanding open problem later summarized in standard references as asking whether sup-norm estimates for \bar\partial hold on convex domains in \mathbb{C}^2. I therefore kept your scope narrow and made the question stand-alone by adding the missing form degree, the \bar\partial-closedness hypothesis on f, the bounded-data/bounded-solution formulation, the domain-dependent constant, and the exact L^\infty estimate. I did not broaden it to general weakly pseudoconvex domains or to Hölder/L^p estimates.
